answer:
Warmup raises the learning rate linearly to its peak, followed by cosine decay to a minimum. The code defines zero-based optimizer-update indexing and both endpoints explicitly; apply the rate before the update. Accumulating several microbatches counts as one optimizer step. A common off-by-one error either misses the peak or never reaches the minimum.

**Mathematical and practical explanation.** After warmup, cosine decay can use $\eta(t)=\eta_{min}+\tfrac12(\eta_{max}-\eta_{min})[1+\cos(\pi u)]$ for progress $u\in[0,1]$. Explicitly map update indices to that interval. Changing batch size or accumulation changes updates per epoch, so schedule comparisons should state whether the budget is tokens, samples, or optimizer steps. [3](https://www.deeplearningbook.org/contents/optimization.html)

For the implementation or system context discussed above, see [1](https://d2l.ai/chapter_optimization/lr-scheduler.html) and [2](https://www.jeremyjordan.me/nn-learning-rate/).
